title: Term life insurance — pure protection
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Term insurance pays a lump sum to your family if you die during the policy term, and nothing if you survive. Because it is pure protection with no investment component, premiums are very low — a healthy 25-year-old can often get a ₹1 crore cover for a few thousand rupees a year. You need it only if someone depends on your income (parents, spouse, children, or a loan co-signer). A common thumb rule is cover of 10–15 times your annual income, plus any outstanding loans. Buy early (premiums rise with age), declare your health, smoking and income details honestly (wrong disclosure can lead to claim rejection), and look at the insurer's claim-settlement ratio. Premiums qualify for 80C in the old regime. Avoid mixing insurance and investment: term plus a mutual fund SIP usually beats endowment or money-back plans.
summary_hinglish: Term insurance mein tumhare na rehne par family ko ek bada amount milta hai, aur zinda rehne par kuch nahi, isliye premium bahut kam. Sirf tab chahiye jab koi tum par depend ho. Cover aam taur par saalana income ka 10-15 guna. Jaldi lo, sab sach declare karo.
summary_hi: टर्म इंश्योरेंस में आपके न रहने पर परिवार को एकमुश्त रकम मिलती है, और जीवित रहने पर कुछ नहीं, इसलिए प्रीमियम बहुत कम होता है। यह तभी ज़रूरी है जब कोई आप पर निर्भर हो। कवर आम तौर पर सालाना आय का 10-15 गुना। जल्दी लें और सब कुछ सच बताएं।
